abstract: The Caenorhabditis elegans neurexin gene nrx-1 encodes both long () and short ({gamma}) isoforms, but how their expression varies across individual neurons remains unclear. Using NeuroPAL and endogenous transcriptional reporters, we generated a nervous system-wide atlas of nrx-1 expression in L4 hermaphrodites. We assessed reporters for one  and two {gamma} transcript groups in 267 identified neurons. The two {gamma} reporters collectively marked a broader set of neurons than the  reporter, and most neurons expressing the  reporter also expressed at least one {gamma} reporter. Among the ventral nerve cord motor neurons examined,  reporter expression was restricted to cholinergic neurons, while one {gamma} reporter was detected exclusively in GABAergic neurons. The other {gamma} reporter was consistently detected in most cholinergic motor neurons and detected in only a subset of GABAergic motor neurons, often variably across animals. In two-fold embryos, this same {gamma} reporter was detected in more neurons than the  reporter. Two upstream regulatory elements contributed to its expression in different neuronal populations. At dorsal nerve cord synapses, disruption of either isoform class reduced NRX-1 fluorescence, with a larger reduction after disruption of the short isoforms. By identifying neurons that express different combinations of long and short neurexins, this atlas provides a starting point for testing where the two isoform classes have distinct synaptic roles and where they may act together.
